title: Graded Nakayama Lemma via the Same Jacobson-Radical Machinery

problemStatement.formal:
\text{Let } R = \bigoplus_{n \ge 0} R_n \text{ be a } \mathbb{N}\text{-graded ring with irrelevant ideal } R_+,\
\text{and } M \text{ a finitely generated graded } R\text{-module bounded below. If } R_+ M = M \text{ then } M = 0.
problemStatement.plain: Nakayama's lemma over a local ring says: if a finitely generated module M satisfies 𝔪M = M (with 𝔪 the maximal ideal), then M = 0. This problem asks for the *graded* analogue, where the graded irrelevant ideal R₊ (elements of positive degree) plays the role of the maximal ideal, and to derive it from the same Jacobson-radical / determinant-trick machinery used for the local-ring forms in the parent proof.

knownResults.goal: State and prove graded Nakayama (R₊ M = M ⟹ M = 0) for an ℕ-graded module.

currentState.focus: Solved: graded Nakayama lemma verified 0-axiom in Proofs/NakayamaLemmaOQ01OQ02.lean.
currentState.nextAction: Follow-up: graded lifting-of-generators corollary; bounded-below ℤ-gradings.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: graded Nakayama proved 0-axiom, NO finite-generation hypothesis needed (bottom-degree argument).
builtItems: projM (Proofs/NakayamaLemmaOQ01OQ02.lean:68): additive degree-i projection M →+ M of an internal graded module, modelled on GradedRing.proj
projM_smul_deg (:83): key vanishing lemma — positive-degree ring element times anything has zero degree-d component when pieces below d are trivial
graded_nakayama (:112): R₊ M = M ⟹ Subsingleton M, no finite generation
insights: The graded case needs NO finite generation: ℕ-grading is bounded below, so a least nonzero degree exists and the determinant/Jacobson machinery is unnecessary — the OQ premise ("same Jacobson-radical machinery") is not the right route.

The degree-d projection must be ADDITIVE, not R-linear: R shifts degrees, so a faithful graded module has additive-submonoid pieces (σM with AddSubmonoidClass), not R-submodules; decompose_smul R-linearity applies only to the degenerate R-submodule model.
SetLike.GradedSMul.smul_mem gives Rᵢ·Mₑ ⊆ M_{i+e}; with VAdd ℕ ℕ = Add.toVAdd, rw [vadd_eq_add] converts i +ᵥ e to i + e.

Submodule.smul_induction_on reduces "projM d vanishes on R₊·⊤" to the r•n generator step; r ∈ irrelevant ⟺ decompose 𝒜 r 0 = 0 (mem_irrelevant_iff + GradedRing.proj_apply) so 0 ∉ support and every homogeneous piece of r has positive degree.
mathlibGaps: No module-level degree projection (GradedRing.proj exists for rings only) — built projM here.
No graded Nakayama lemma in Mathlib (only the local/FG Nakayama in RingTheory.Nakayama).
nextSteps: Graded lifting-of-generators corollary via graded_nakayama on M/⟨lifts⟩.
